user.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
Shelf is a small local reading list. Run `npm start` and open http://127.0.0.1:3000.

The home page shows what you are currently reading and what you have finished, with a form to add a title, author, and notes. Mark finished moves a book to the finished list. Each book has its own page at `/books/<id>` with the title, author, notes, and a link you can copy.

Books are stored in `data/books.json` and stay there after a restart. There are no accounts. It listens only on this computer, so a shared link works here. Set `HOST=0.0.0.0` if someone else on the network needs to open it. Anyone who can reach the server can also open the full shelf and change books.

`npm test` passed, 9 tests, exit 0. A live check also added a book, opened its link, and marked it finished.

tool_steps.assistant: I'll start by checking the workspace so the book tracker matches what's already here, then build a small app that stores books in a JSON file.

{"action":"run","command":"set -e
base=http://127.0.0.1:3456
echo '--- home ---'

echo '--- finish ---'
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -X POST "$base/books/$id/finish" --data 'next=/'
echo '--- after finish ---'
python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("/tmp/shelf-smoke/books.json"))["books"][0]["status"])'
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'direct-link %{http_code}\n' "$base/books/$id"
echo '--- missing ---'
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'missing %{http_code}\n' "$base/books/not-a-book""}
